annotation.title_clean: Autonomous surgical robotic systems and the liability dilemma
annotation.title_en: Autonomous surgical robotic systems and the liability dilemma
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Jamjoom, A.A.B.; Jamjoom, A.M.A.; Thomas, J.P.; Palmisciano, P.; Kerr, K.; Collins, J.W.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed report of the iRobotSurgeon survey (2,191 respondents, 78 countries) on who the public blames when autonomous surgical robots harm patients. Blame shifts from surgeons to manufacturers as autonomy rises, but no consensus emerges for full autonomy, and surgeons still bear blame, suggesting "moral crumple zone" risks.
key_provisions_or_claims: Public blame shifts from surgeon to manufacturer as robot autonomy increases
No consensus on responsibility for harm from fully autonomous surgical systems
Surgeons are still blamed even with no decision-making role, supporting 'moral crumple zone' concerns
Survey of 2,191 respondents across 78 countries with five hypothetical scenarios
Findings highlight need for clear liability frameworks for autonomous surgical robots
